description: Q01 (ffw-gmq) offline Virtual House harness: every case of tests/q01/cases.json, judged by scripts/test/q00/q01_case.py from the log of the centrally run speaker lib tests (FFW_Q01_LOG). Without that log every case is blocked, never passed. The authoritative floor is derived separately by scripts/test/q00/q01_floor.py from the case table and the Rust sources.

Q01.AC1.text: Check samples and state, not log strings alone.

Q01.AC2.text: Race two real adapter interfaces replacing sources and retrying relative volume; assert sample/state revisions.

Q01.AC3.text: Separate unit/mock simulation from full-system and hardware evidence.

cases.description: [bring-up, positive] a node is brought up through the real readiness sequence and reaches ready; the HAL itself still refuses an unmute before priming; the readiness spec for the clock is pinned to N03's configuration
[bring-up, negative] a weakened driver threshold and a node that skips its own gate on an unlocked clock are each refused by name
[timeline, positive] a block's start maps back to its scheduled frame however long the campaign runs; a locked node sounds at the admitted start and not before; the simulated member clocks are pinned

[clock faults, negative] a suspend, a clock leap, an unadmitted node, and unsolicited, replayed, stale and wrong-leader probes each mute or change nothing, and never produce audio; request bases differ per member and boot
[campaign, positive] the mixed S1/S2 fleet streams every block of every member, measures a skew from independent clocks, checks every channel against the shadow render, and is deterministic
[campaign, negative] a corrupted sample in any channel and a missing final block are caught

[campaign, negative] an unmeasured skew is not a pass: a mostly muted house, a refused member, a campaign that compared nothing and a house with one participant make no synchronisation claim they cannot support
[fencing, positive] the fencing probe drives the real session and the independent oracle accepts it; a rejected command does not adopt its epoch
[fencing, limit] KNOWN LIMIT, pinned: a valid command at an undeclared epoch is still applied

[diagnostics, positive] a planted fault leaves itself and its causal chain in the log; the default sink bounds a burst but never limits a healthy stream; an unavailable, full, zero-capacity or tiny sink changes nothing else

[playout, negative] the real N04 engine decides every block as the seeded schedule says; a late block, a reordered pair, a previous-epoch datagram and a clock leap each move exactly what they should and nothing else; the adapter's own controls: on-time and reordered blocks play their sent bytes, a duplicate plays once, a missing block and a long loss are concealed by the contract's rule, a late or stale packet is refused and changes nothing, an unusable or leaped clock is never latched, and the oracle trips on a send time stamped as an arrival time

[negotiation, positive] every member's stream comes out of an N01 negotiation; each session has its own key; a member that answers with an unsupported version or cannot take a full block is refused and muted with its cause; peer identities and nonces are valid, distinct and deterministic

[source replacement, positive] two real adapters racing to replace the source admit exactly one in either order and the house cuts over at one frame; the program each block carried is read from the bytes that sounded; each stream generation has its own engine, an old-stream datagram still in flight at the commit is authenticated on arrival by the old generation's own receiver copy and played (the rebound receiver alone would refuse it), rapid generations are capped only by the ledger, and a fresh trusted group epoch resumes with a new stream without relabeling any old queued generation

[source replacement, negative] a replaced adapter that keeps publishing is refused by the gate; a datagram of the replaced stream is refused by the rebound receiver; a planted source fault with no source change is an error; arrival-time refusals are made by the layer that owns the check (N01 replay, MAC, the generation's interval, a retired or unknown stream), an authentic out-of-interval datagram cannot poison a replay window, a trusted group-epoch change fences every stale generation, and a source change the ledger cannot fund is refused whole with the old stream still authenticating and only the selected expected refusal accepted

[relative volume, positive] the real G03 endpoint and N02 channel: a plain-SOAP retry applies again, a tailnet retry with the same number applies once and reports the volume as it is now, a stale revision is refused and remembered, a bad proof changes nothing, clamps still move the revision, a group step moves the group

[relative volume, positive] the volume plan the contract predicts: the race plan and the reference plan, an invalid plan is refused (with a valid control), an unfinished plan is not a clean run, the harness key store follows the secret-store contract

[relative volume, negative] a tailnet retry sent as a new command and a stale revision a client refreshes are each named by the oracle (adapter level and whole campaign), each with its unplanted control; a planted volume fault with no plan is refused

[relative volume, positive] the race around a source change does what the contract predicts and sounds exactly like a reference that sets the same volumes directly; a campaign with no plan reports none and sounds the same every time

[sound evidence, control] the sample digest tells volume trajectories apart (a wrong reference differs in that member only); the digest of silence equals the independently computed value; the endpoint member renders and a mono-routed member does not

[sound evidence, positive] under the Asymmetric source every member renders sound; the source keeps the left channel and its mono mix never cancels; a member the gate never let sound is not asked to have rendered anything
[sound evidence, limit] LIMIT 1, pinned: under the original opposed source a mono-routed member renders only zeros and that is not a failure
[sound evidence, negative] a member handed silence fails the campaign by name under Asymmetric, and passes every other oracle under the original source (which is why the question is asked)

[diagnostics, positive] (added by the N03 redaction fix, 4611dd2) a campaign's diagnostic events name a member only in member_id and in no free-text field; a keyed sink holds no raw member or group label in any field or in the JSONL; a planted fault names its member as a field and never in its text; a failure that names no member is recorded as the house's with its whole text as the cause; redacting a failure replaces every member label and names the first member it mentions; the redacted labels are the members the campaign has
[diagnostics, negative] (added by the N03 redaction fix, 4611dd2) the leak scan names the free-text field a raw member id is put back in

[end of campaign, positive] the SOAP skeleton call is retired: every campaign ends with an absolute group volume set through the real endpoint over local legacy SOAP; it applies, a plain-SOAP repeat leaves the volume where it was (an absolute set is safe to repeat), only the group moves, and the report records it

[end of campaign, negative] an out-of-range group volume is refused (UPnP 402) with no effect and the boundary values are accepted; a set the endpoint refuses fails the end-of-campaign step by name, each against its control
[measurement, measurement] what every member renders under each source at the --virtual-house campaign: one Q01-MEMBER record per member and source, judged from the log
[measurement, measurement] the SilentInput plant is named for every one of the five members, with its remove-the-plant control: one Q01-PLANT record per run, judged from the log
